paragraphs: Rav Naḥman bar Ushpazti, to Rav Pappa, Ta'anit 3. Arukh, Bar, explains Ushpazti as Rav Pappa's mother's name; its reading is Ushparti. Yuḥasin understood Rav Naḥman, rather than Rav Pappa, as Ushpazti's son, otherwise why include him among Naḥmans? Ta'anit 24b: Rav Pappa decreed a fast, felt weak and tasted something, swallowing a bowl of porridge. He prayed but rain did not come. Rav Naḥman bar Ushpazti asked whether swallowing another bowl might bring rain. Heilprin reports that Ein Yaakov reads Rav Naḥman bar Oshaya. BaMeh Ishah has Rav Naḥman bar Oshaya, but I entered him as Rav Natan bar Oshaya, since you do not find Naḥman bar Oshaya; it is a scribal error (see his entry). Perhaps Ein Yaakov too should read Rav Natan bar Oshaya. I wished to defend Arukh's naming Rav Pappa after his mother, since his father was not known (see his entry), but I raised an objection to that argument—see R. Zeira. In any event Yuḥasin erred in including Rav Naḥman bar Ushpazta.
